Canonical ABI bridge boundary: the proxy and dispatch marshalling (`_bridge_arg_ser`/`_arg_extract`/`_ret_deser`/`_ret_ser`, the hand-encoded `Result` and `_bridge_serde_ok`) is ported since item 391 and held to byte agreement by emit_rust_corpus/bridge_types.rvl. Component construction fallbacks: residuals cover absent/malformed service or requirement declarations, effectful-method routing, configuration-use alternatives, and older constructor selection. The corpus exercises valid service traits, scalar config, pure provide methods, and direct free-function calls. emit_rust_corpus/teardown_compensate.rvl (item 391) reaches 2 more statements each of `_emit_component`, `_emit_component_new` and `_emit_components`: the teardown begin and commit lines on both provider paths, and the module's teardown preamble. emit_rust_corpus/intercept_metadata.rvl (item 391, the intercept port) reaches more of this group: `_emit_component_new` 21 -> 7.

Concrete->Any boxing coercion (`_coerce_any_arg`): a concrete scalar flowing into an `Any`/`Value` parameter is boxed as `Value::new(serde_json::Value::from(..))` (native `compile_to`, #106/#98). The firing path is not reached by the byte-agreement corpus yet: a concrete->Any document would need the self-host `emit_rust.rvl` call renderer to mirror the same boxing (a tracked follow-up), or the two tiers diverge on it. Recorded until that mirror + corpus case land. The count rose 3 -> 5 when the non-finite-`Float` arm was added: `serde_json::Value::from(f64)` maps a non-finite float to `Null` silently, so a `Float` argument boxes through a checked `serde_json::Number::from_f64` and refuses the `None` rather than substituting a different value. The `Some` arm is corpus-reachable in principle once the mirror lands. The `None` arm is structurally unreachable from ANY static corpus document: a non-finite `Float` has no literal spelling (the frontend refuses it, item 312) and arises only at runtime, through IEEE true division. Recorded rather than chased, because the corpus case cannot exist before the mirror does. The count rose 5 -> 7 with the RETURN and `??`-DEFAULT positions: a declared `-> Any` erases to the same opaque `Value`, so returning a concrete scalar from such a function is the identical E0308 the argument position had, and an `Opt[Any] ?? <scalar>` default fills the same slot through `unwrap_or_else`. Both route through this function, and both are blocked from the corpus by the same missing mirror. The `List[Any]` arm arrives with them: a `Vec<Value>` boxes as the JSON array `stdlib/value.rvl`'s `value_list` reads back, the one container with a canonical image, and it is the coercion that let `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl` itself build as rust (the Stage-4 precondition).

Demand-selected formatting helpers: canonical Float interpolation and record/timer preambles are emitted only when those deferred runtime features are present. The teardown preamble left this group with item 391: emit_rust_corpus/teardown_compensate.rvl selects it. Ordinary string interpolation and checked arithmetic are covered without selecting these helper bodies.

Explicit invalid-input guards: accepted frontend IR contains no unresolved holes; `_refuse_holes` and its walker make such direct or stale IR fail loudly instead of generating Rust. `_refuse_deferred_emissions` used to be recorded here and is now recorded beside `_refuse_validated_emissions`, with the reason both carry (issue #1431).

Extern-declared compensate (item 254, issue #1592): `_emit_compensations` adds the compensation an emission extern declares to the ones an `emit` registers, `_reaches_declared` and `_declared_call` register one for a call in any other position of a provide method (a `let`, a `return`, an argument, a nested operand, an `if` arm) as a block expression, and `_as_fn_call` re-spells that slot (lowered in the pure-expression call dialect) as a component `fn` node, at the activation body, a provide-method body and a timer firing. A corpus document carrying such an extern cannot be a byte-agreement case: selfhost/emit_rust.rvl ports the site-spelled registration (item 391) but not the declared one, and names a document that declares one with a `<<DEFER-declared-compensate>>` marker. `_emit_compensations` 4 -> 3: emit_rust_corpus/teardown_compensate.rvl reaches its site-clause statement. The behaviour is pinned and executed against real cordis-rs by backends/rust/test_emit_rust.py::test_extern_declared_compensation_registers_at_every_site.

Extern-only boundary: these statements build extern config bindings, reject missing @rs bodies, and emit color-erased extern declarations. The corpus covers ordinary native Rust extern bodies but not runtime config scaffolding or invalid declarations.

In-file test and lifecycle harness generation is outside the self-host module emitter: these branches create runtime load/unload/call/advance/no-residue drivers and fault-test rejection rather than library functions. Since item 391 the pure `test` section is ported: selfhost/emit_rust.rvl emits each block as a `#[test] fn`, held to byte agreement by emit_rust_corpus/in_file_tests.rvl, so `_emit_v3_tests` keeps only its `continue` past a lifecycle test, which `_emit_v3` never hands it (it splits the lifecycle tests off first).

Item 421 F5: a document that declares a `Secret[T]` AND returns a `Result` from a provided method serializes the Err half through this funnel rather than `_result_to_json`, because the failure text is the one thing crossing the seam that has to be scrubbed. No corpus document does both: the rust byte-agreement corpus reaches the bridge (service.rvl, services_multi.rvl) but holds no document declaring a `Secret[T]` at all, and the port (selfhost/emit_rust.rvl) carries no `_SECRET_MODE` and emits no funnel call, so a secret-bearing bridge document could not be a byte-identical corpus case. The reference half is pinned by tests/test_rust_seam_failure_scrub.py::test_secret_mode_emits_the_funnel_and_the_shared_marker.

item 421 F6 (the rust half): the declared-`Secret[T]` runtime secret registry. `_declares_secret` scans the IR for a surviving `Secret[T]` marking (service param `secret`, extern `secret_return`, config-field `secret`) to gate `_SECRET_MODE`; `_emit_secret_registry` is the glob import of the runner crate's registry (`placement_runner/src/confidential.rs`, a fixed part of the runner so its own console channels read the same process-global) emitted into the crate once under that mode; `_secret_config_fields`/`_secret_config_mark` register a `Secret[T]` config field at the head of the plugin closure, the register-at-load shape the go tier uses; `_secret_method_params` registers a `Secret[T]` provide-method parameter at the method head; `_stream_host_rust` funnels the host-trace choke point `revl_stream_record` through `revl_redact_text`. The door DISPATCH is `_secret_mark_call`/`_secret_result_lines`: item 421 F6(f) routes a `Secret[T]` by its DECLARED type, because the old generic `T: std::fmt::Display` bound has no impl for `Vec<u8>` (`Bytes`), `Vec<String>` (`List[Str]`) or cordis `Value`, so a non-scalar `Secret[T]` composition emitted a crate that did not compile. `Str`/`Int`/`Int32`/`Float`/`Bool` keep the `Display` door; `Bytes` takes `revl_mark_secret_bytes`/`revl_secret_result_bytes` (decoded text + json array + Debug, mirroring go's F6(e) byte-slice branch); everything else takes `revl_mark_secret_encoded`/`revl_secret_result_encoded` (`Debug`, the one formatter every lowering implements). Item 421 F6(i) makes the DOOR walk the declared shape at emit time (`_secret_face_lines`), registering every reachable leaf through the door that leaf's own type takes: the container's own face is not the coverage, because `revl_redact_text` matches an exact needle and a sink writing one element on its own crosses verbatim. A shape the walk cannot decompose keeps the container face alone. No rust corpus document declares a `Secret[T]`, so the positive branches never run, and selfhost/emit_rust.rvl does not port secret redaction (item-429(d)): a corpus document reaching them would flip the byte-agreement oracle red rather than close this gap. The reference half is pinned by backends/rust/test_rust_secret_registry.py (the door-shape tests plus the `#[needs_cargo]` build-and-scrub harness). Item 421 F6(j) caps the walk at the go tier's `depth > 8` so a recursive record has a base case: without it the emitter died on a legal program (`type Node = { next: Opt[Node] }`) instead of emitting, because the walk recurses the DECLARED type and `Opt` stores its payload inline. Item 421 F6(o) removes the depth cap: it was a confidentiality regression in the walk that exists to prevent one, because it terminates the recursion but also stops REGISTERING, so the leaves of any declared shape nested deeper than the cap were never registered as their own text and crossed verbatim in every sink `revl_redact_text` covers. A nine-level `Secret[Map[Str, ...]]` extern is admitted with zero `revl_mark_secret` and its leaf crosses verbatim (proved in a real crate, RC 101). The bound is now the PATH of declared types the walk is on, which cuts a cycle exactly where the shape re-enters itself and leaves every legal shape's leaves registered at any depth, `path` being per-branch so two sibling fields of one type are both walked. One statement arrives with it, so `_secret_face_lines` is re-recorded 37 to 38 uncovered statements under the same item 421 F6 rust reason. Item 421 F6(p) extends the walk to VARIANT cases, the one declared shape item 421 F6(i) left out: the walk decomposed the four generic heads and `record` and then returned `[]`, so a `Secret[Variant]` registered the container's own `Debug` face and nothing inside it, while the plainest thing an author writes with an ADT is one case's payload, a different string that crossed every sink `revl_redact_text` covers. Rust was the outlier of the three tiers again -- go reaches the payload through the struct a variant emits and py through `_members`'s `__slots__` probe, and rust has neither reflection nor a case arm. The branch emits `match &{expr} { <Enum>::<Case>(_revl_leaf<depth>) => { <payload walk> } ... _ => {} }`; the scrutinee is borrowed because the origin door returns the owned value, the case name is mangled like the definition, the `_` arm keeps the match exhaustive over nullary and re-entrant cases, and a payload with no leaf leaves the container face as the whole coverage. Fifteen statements arrive with it, so `_secret_face_lines` is re-recorded 38 to 54 uncovered statements under the same item 421 F6 rust reason. Item 481 makes the `Map` branch walk the declared KEY type beside the declared value type: a map's keys are values the program put in the container, and every tier that handled a record did so in its own separate branch, so the record rule the `values()`-only walk cited does not reach this site. Five statements arrive with it, so `_secret_face_lines` is re-recorded 54 to 59 uncovered statements under the same item 421 F6 rust reason.

Ownership and string-view alternatives: residuals are the computed/non-atomic argument refusal, unknown or function-typed clone safety nets, positional char-view threading, and undo recloning branches. Pure-v3 expression and statement residuals: explicit refusals remain for host/format/optional/update/spawn expressions, Map and positional-string/mutating collection builtins, destructuring, empty-Vec accumulator optimization, recursive collection persistence, Float interpolation, and malformed operators/nodes. Covered cases include all ordinary scalar/list/record/ADT expressions, widening, calls, conditional receivers, bare returns, and supported builtins. Issue #957's `Map` subscript arm adds one statement: no corpus document indexes a `Map`, and one that did would flip the byte-agreement oracle RED rather than close the gap, because selfhost/emit_rust.rvl has no map-subscript arm (item-429(d)); the reference half is pinned by tests/test_cross_tier_execution.py. Its own residual statement is the `@self` fallback for a receiver the corpus never leaves untyped; the same missing mirror keeps a corpus document from reaching it, because `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl` carries no inference layer of its own. emit_rust_corpus/by_value_reuse.rvl (item 391) reaches one more `_v3_infer_type` arm (the `match` arm-body type), 4 -> 3: selfhost/emit_rust.rvl now mirrors the inference arms the by-value rules read (literal, index, field, record, `match`, stdlib-method result).

Realm routing and child instances require intercept JSON metadata, deterministic realm identities, router structs, spawn handles, and runtime child configuration. The self-host emitter explicitly defers isolate/intercept/routes/spawn. emit_rust_corpus/intercept_metadata.rvl (item 391, the intercept port) reaches more of this group: `_intercept_json_lit` 18 -> 2, `_intercept_json_type` 34 -> 3.

Record/variant context invariants: the remaining branches diagnose duplicate or ambiguous record shapes and constructors, malformed pattern arity, and recursive boxing edges. The self-host Rust slice supports the covered unique non-recursive records and ADTs but deliberately does not mirror recursive boxing. emit_rust_corpus/bridge_types.rvl (item 391) reaches 2 more of `_V3Ctx._disambiguate_record`'s statements.

Recursive struct-field boxing (issue #919): the second half of the boxing pass, which puts a recursive STRUCT-field edge behind a `Box` (E0072) and then unboxes it where it is read (E0308 — Rust does not auto-deref a `Box` field in value position). `_inline_cycle_target` decides which wrapper types can carry the edge; `_boxed_field_read` unboxes it at the read site. Both are ENTERED on every corpus document, because the pass runs unconditionally over the document's types, so their headers and early exits execute; the struct-field arms below those exits are reached only by a document carrying such an edge. The rust byte-agreement corpus cannot hold one: the port (selfhost/emit_rust.rvl) carries no boxing pass at all — no `boxed_cases`/`boxed_fields`, no `_recursive_boxed_edges` — so the reference would emit a deref the port does not and there is no byte-identical oracle to hold over it. The recursive-edge regression lives in tests/test_emit_rust_opt_recursion_919.py instead, which asserts the emitted text directly. emit_rust_corpus/by_value_reuse.rvl (item 391) declares a record with a `List[Str]` field, which drives `_inline_cycle_target` 4 statements further before its early exit, 13 -> 9.

`_refuse_deferred_emissions` and `_refuse_validated_emissions` in backends/rust/emit.py are the same wrapper around a shared refusal in `revl.session_commit` and `revl.validated_boundary`. The 8 statements left in each are the `except ModuleNotFoundError` standalone-import bootstrap, which puts src/ on sys.path and imports `revl` again. It runs only when emit.py is executed as a script with `revl` not importable. That is an invocation mode, not an input, so no corpus document and no refusal document can reach it, and these 16 statements stay recorded by design rather than as backlog. The RevlError-to-EmitError translation in both wrappers used to be recorded here too and is reached now, by tests/fixtures/emit_rust_refusals/deferred_emission_call.rvl and validated_emission_operation.rvl (issue #1431). Measured 10 -> 8 in each wrapper.

`_render_expr` residuals, in two families no mirrored-corpus document reaches. (1) The refusal/fallback arms for host/format/optional/update/spawn expressions, Map and positional-string/mutating collection builtins, destructuring, empty-Vec accumulators, Float interpolation and malformed nodes; the corpus covers the ordinary scalar/list/record/ADT expressions, widening, calls, conditional receivers, bare returns and supported builtins. (2) item 333: the `method == "length"` and `method == "slice"` branches that serve those builtins through a threaded `&[char]` view (`{view}.len()` and `{view}.iter().skip(a).take(b-a)` instead of `revl_length`'s `chars().count()` and `revl_slice`'s `chars().skip` front walks). Reaching them needs a bare-parameter positional `slice`/index that SEEDS the view (`_STR_VIEW_SEED_BUILTINS` -> `_str_params_indexed` -> `_compute_char_views`), and the self-host port deliberately DEFERS that whole positional char-view family: `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl` threads no `&[char]` param, emits `revl_length()` for length and has no string `slice` builtin at all (it renders `<<UNSUPPORTED-BUILTIN:slice>>`). Because the line-coverage corpus IS the byte-agreement corpus (`tests/test_selfhost_emit_rust.py::CORPUS`), a seeding document would force the port to diverge, so it cannot be added until that family is ported. The seeding machinery itself is already recorded under the string-view-alternatives reason (`_compute_char_views`, `_char_view_args`, `_str_params_indexed.walk`). (3) issue #919: the two `return` statements that unbox a recursive STRUCT-field read — `f"(*{place}.{field}).clone()"` at the by-value-reuse site and `f"(*{target}.{field})"` at the value site. Their guards (`_boxed_field_read`) run on every field read, so the tests execute; only the returns wait on a document with a recursive struct-field edge. A corpus document cannot supply one for the same reason as (2): the port carries no boxing pass, so the reference would emit a deref the port does not. The read half of the pass is recorded under the recursive-struct-field-boxing reason (`_boxed_field_read`, `_inline_cycle_target`). Issue #957's `Map` subscript arm adds one statement: no corpus document indexes a `Map`, and one that did would flip the byte-agreement oracle RED rather than close the gap, because selfhost/emit_rust.rvl has no map-subscript arm (item-429(d)); the reference half is pinned by tests/test_cross_tier_execution.py. Item 130 §4.5 adds two statements: the `replay(…)` refusal on a `Stream.source()` declaration this tier does not lower. Issue #1734 reaches the component-position property `.length` (a `field` node marked `sized_length`, rendered through `revl_length`) with emit_rust_corpus/comp_str_builtin.rvl, so that return no longer counts here.
Standalone transport boundary: the oracle imports emit directly, so module execution, argparse/stdin/file output, and separately requested Cargo manifest generation are not entered.

Stream runtime boundary: these paths recognize subscribe/merge/next, select the stream head, track subscription binds, and reject unlowered stream policy/stage forms. Since item 130 Slice 5 the same boundary carries the typed-event half: `_uses_stream_event` asks whether any component iterates a typed event (the document predicate that pulls the contract, and with it the stream host runtime, even when the subscription arrives as a required service) and `_stream_event_host_rust` materializes the `EventContract` schema-and-dedup preamble. Both are reached only by a document holding an `on <Event> as <e> in <sub>` handler, which no corpus document does. The self-host Rust emitter has no stream runtime representation. item 130 Slice 2 lowered the derived-stream combinator chain here (`_stream_chain` nests the `map`/`filter`/`take` links inside the subscription's acquisition and `_stream_stage_arrow` renders each pure transform against the tier's string item type); both are on the same stream-holding path and so are uncovered for the same reason. `_refuse_unlowered_stream_surface` drops from 7 to 5 because the combinator arm it used to carry is gone. `_refuse_unlowered_stream_surface` goes back from 2 to 4: item 130 §4.5 puts the `replay(…)` refusal beside the surviving `drain` one. The two are refused for different reasons — the window for the deterministic clock this tier does not carry, replay for the recovery surface (§4.9) that lives on py — and neither is reachable from a corpus document, because a stream-holding document cannot be one. item 130's required-`Stream[T]` coeffect refusal (`_refuse_required_stream`) used to be recorded here on the same grounds, and is not any more: a corpus document cannot reach it, but a REFUSAL document can, and tests/fixtures/emit_rust_refusals/required_stream_coeffect.rvl does (issue #1419).

Validated-IR and scalar formatting fallbacks: these statements reject malformed refs/signatures/identifiers, non-finite floats, absent or unknown types, invalid literal nodes, and unsupported escape/default forms. Accepted typed identifiers, scalar defaults, widening and ASCII/control escaping are positively covered. emit_rust_corpus/bridge_types.rvl (item 391) reaches 1 more of `_rust_type`'s statements.

Version and document-shape guards: emit rejects malformed/unknown IR, _emit_v1/_emit_v2 are legacy paths outside the mirrored v3 contract, and the residual _emit_v3 statements handle empty documents plus test/lifecycle sections delegated to their explicit boundaries. emit_rust_corpus/intercept_metadata.rvl (item 391, the intercept port) reaches more of this group: `_emit_v2` 6 -> 1, `emit` 3 -> 2.

Witnessed effect and compensation runtime: these branches detect transactional bodies, emit setup/acquire/undo registration, reclone captured locals, and begin/commit teardown frames. The self-host port has no WAL/frame ABI and explicitly defers the witnessed half rather than emitting a partial transaction. The compensation half is ported since item 391 and held to byte agreement by emit_rust_corpus/teardown_compensate.rvl, which reaches `_emit_teardown_begin`, `_emit_teardown_commit`, `_emit_compensation_registration` and `_emit_activation_compensation` in full, 6 more of `_method_body_lines`'s statements and 1 more each of `_body_has_compensation`'s and `_method_bodies_have_compensation`'s. What is left of those is the witnessed half, the extern-declared compensation (issue #1592) and the component-`if` walk, which no document can reach because a component `if` is a guard that holds only `fail` (G6). emit_rust_corpus/method_control_flow.rvl (item 391) reaches 5 more of `_method_body_lines`'s statements, 35 -> 30: the top-level control-flow arm (issue #548).
